text: Define prolificness as distinct 2021–2024 snapshot works on which the researcher has a Columbia or included child-institution affiliation on their own authorship. Take exactly 80, breaking a cutoff tie by ascending stable author ID. The collaboration graph joins those 80 if they coauthored a snapshot work in the period, even if neither has a Columbia affiliation on that particular work; edge weight is the number of distinct shared works. Include isolates and all snapshot work types.

Use distinct 2021–2024 inclusive snapshot works (all types, no extra filters). Eligibility/count is a matching affiliation on the specific authorship with institutions.is_columbia (Columbia I78577930 and four snapshot children); join affiliation rows on work ID, stable author ID and byline order and deduplicate (work ID, author ID), excluding unresolved null author IDs. Rank by that count descending, then ascending stable OpenAlex author ID (text), taking exactly 80. Profile names label nodes, with byline name fallback. Optional total snapshot count ignores author affiliation but stays within the same snapshot and years. Edges are simple undirected pairs (lexically smaller ID first), weighted by distinct shared snapshot works regardless of either author's affiliation; keep all 80 nodes independently of edges.

Keep T1 selection/rank and T2 weights as supplied: ranking uses each author's distinct qualifying Columbia-affiliated snapshot works; an edge counts distinct snapshot works shared by its endpoints regardless of their affiliation on those works. Degree is the number of other selected authors joined by an edge; weighted degree sums original shared-work counts over neighbors (a work can contribute to multiple ties). Component colors use stable component anchor IDs (best-ranked member per component); isolates are singleton components, displayed neutrally in a separate panel.

Report the top degree tiers through the fifth author, retaining everyone tied at that boundary; report the five strongest edges by original shared-work count. Use competition ranks for ties, T1 rank for ordering within a degree tie, and endpoint IDs for ordering within a tie in edge strength.

Reuse exactly T1's 80 researchers and T2's original weighted ties. For bundling, infer a single primary OpenAlex field from the plurality of each author's own Columbia-affiliated 2021–2024 works with a usable primary topic, then choose the plurality primary-topic subfield within that field (one vote per distinct work, stable taxonomy IDs break ties). If a work's primary topic is unavailable, use a documented validated equivalent or treat it as unclassified. Keep unclassified researchers visible and do not treat missing classifications as evidence of a cross-field collaboration. Roles reflect publication mix, not departmental affiliation.

Freeze T1 author IDs, names and ranks and use the same 2021–2024 snapshot and all work types. The classification universe is distinct (author_id, work_id) with authorships.is_columbia true on that author's own byline, not the broader snapshot-work universe used for unchanged T2 ties. T3 reports zero mismatches between this marker and the parent/child affiliation criteria.

A usable vote requires a primary topic ID matching the snapshot taxonomy. Use works.primary_field when present, resolving it to a unique taxonomy field ID and checking agreement with the primary topic hierarchy. If absent, use the matched primary topic's validated taxonomy field; a missing ID, unmatched topic or hierarchy conflict is a nonvote. Derive subfield ID and label from that same topic, requiring agreement with the explicit subfield when present. No secondary topics or alternative taxonomy. No-vote authors retain explicit Unclassified labels and null taxonomy IDs.

Count one vote per eligible distinct author–work pair. Choose plurality field among classified works and then plurality subfield only within that field; sort on votes descending and numeric stable taxonomy ID ascending. Report winner/runner-up counts and shares, tie size, and separate close non-ties (positive lead no more than five percentage points of applicable votes with an actual runner-up). Coverage denominator is all eligible affiliated works; field dominance denominator is classified works; subfield dominance denominator is votes in the assigned field. Edge diagnostics count unchanged T2 tie rows once; cross-field means both endpoints classified and assigned field IDs differ.

Use T6's single plurality field among distinct Columbia-affiliated 2021–2024 author-work votes with validated primary topics, then plurality subfield within that field; numeric stable taxonomy ID ascending breaks ties. Verify against T7. Edge classes compare assigned field IDs first, then subfield IDs within the same field; a missing assignment would be an explicit separate bucket. These are author classifications, not classifications of shared works. Count each undirected T2 pair once; retain its original shared-work weight.

Use contiguous taxonomy-ID-ordered field and subfield blocks, then alphabetize researchers by case-folded display name (stable author ID breaks ties). Use deterministic radial spacing with extra gaps at group boundaries; there is no stochastic layout or crossing optimization. Route every tie through the lowest common ancestor in the taxonomy tree; class shares divide by all ties in the stated scope, while field-pair shares also provide the cross-field-only denominator. Rank pairs by tie count descending then numeric field IDs ascending; preserve all observed pairs.

For both views, highlight distinct direct T2 neighbors of exact OpenAlex author ID A5057686070, matching either endpoint, excluding the selected ID and imposing no additional shared-work threshold. Use T1 for names, T4 for degree validation, and order the output by descending T2 shared snapshot works then ascending author ID.
